# Reviewed base corrections

The architecture manifests pin official NCCL 2.29.7 artifacts to match Torch 2.13 metadata. ARM64 additionally reproduces the cuSPARSELt packaging-only repair described in the sibling directory. No EP/M2N compatibility is asserted: this worker uses one GPU and a dense model with no KV connector. LMCache has no reverse dependencies and its unused lazy connector is removed. Six unused Ubuntu apt administration packages are removed explicitly, without autoremove. The architecture Python inventories and OS inventories describe the complete resulting baseline after the separately recorded 32 Ubuntu security upgrades. Build verification rejects every unlisted inventory difference. Final overlay provenance captures the full inherited Python closure as well as added wheels.

AMD64 additionally removes the entire orphan `mooncake-transfer-engine==0.3.13.post1` distribution, including its Python namespace, auditwheel native directory and console scripts. No installed distribution declares it, and the fixed text worker leaves both KV and encoder transfer configurations disabled. Its native etcd wrapper carried the additional Go findings; individual libraries or package metadata are never removed selectively. The AMD64 build gate denies and records Mooncake import attempts while importing the actual LLM, sampling, decoder and engine-argument paths.

The AMD64 upstream base's PyPI TorchCodec 0.17.0 wheel requires CUDA 13 libraries despite its CUDA 12.9 Torch profile. The exact official PyTorch `0.17.0+cu126` wheel preserves the upstream release and uses CUDA 12 SONAMEs supplied by this base. Its public URL, size and SHA256 are pinned in `amd64-gpu.json`. This is a narrowly validated text-worker import correction, not a general claim that mixed CUDA toolkit variants support every media operation. No extra CUDA libraries, model changes or native source patch are involved. Native ARM64 does not receive either AMD-only correction.
